# CASEs with `tags` `endosymbiosis`

*Topics — What a work is about. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Endosymbiosis and reductive evolution** — how one organism comes to live inside another and depend on it, and how that ends — reductive genome evolution by drift, deletional bias or adaptive loss (including the Black Queen dependencies of free-living microbes), complementary loss across partners, nested symbioses and symbiont splitting and replacement, endosymbiotic gene transfer, protein import and host control of transmission, organellogenesis and organelle loss, and eukaryogenesis. The ecology of a partnership is ecology (ADR-055).

Essential amino-acid pathways need gene products from both bacteria and the insect ([LIT-1565](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1565.md)). At least 22 genes the insect acquired from other bacteria, none from Tremblaya, fill symbiont gaps ([LIT-1569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1569.md)), and the inner symbiont has been replaced several times across mealybugs while those genes persisted ([LIT-1572](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1572.md)). The record's reading of Wilson and Barker reports Godfrey-Smith placing the pair as both an organism and a Darwinian individual ([NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md)). Used as the case of high mutual dependence and high reproductive cohesion reached through reduction, with no gene transfer to the host reported in the works it rests on. | Proposed |

Used as the case where host control emerges by gene transfer and import. | Proposed |
